name: carbon_leakage_net_effect
description: Condition under which a national carbon price produces a negative net effect on the consumption-based footprint of a tradable product: the shift term must exceed the abatement term. Includes the general formula, the tipping point, and five worked examples (tomatoes CH/DE, steel-like).

triples.name: consumption-based footprint
triples.description: greenhouse gas emissions attributed to domestic consumption of a product, regardless of production location; contrast with the territorial (UNFCCC production-based) inventory

triples.name: abatement term
triples.description: emission change from reduced domestic production intensity, applied to the initial domestic share: (1 - m0) * (eA - e0); non-positive

triples.name: shift term
triples.description: emission change from production relocating to the foreign producer: (m - m0) * (eB - eA); non-negative when the foreign producer is dirtier

triples.name: leakage rate
triples.description: L = foreign emission increase divided by domestic emission decrease; the net effect is negative exactly when L exceeds 100 percent

triples.name: tipping import increase
triples.description: critical increase of the import share dm* above which the net effect turns negative: dm* = (1 - m0) * (e0 - eA) / (eB - eA)

triples.name: crude steel
triples.description: the traded product of the steel example

triples.name: oil-heated greenhouse
triples.description: winter greenhouse production heated by fuel oil

triples.name: heat-pump greenhouse
triples.description: winter greenhouse production heated by an electric heat pump; the abated domestic route of the tomato examples

triples.name: blast furnace route
triples.description: primary steel production via the coal-based blast furnace and basic oxygen furnace route

triples.name: European Union
triples.description: the domestic producer of the steel example, at the average intensity of its blast furnace route
kilograms of CO2 equivalent per kilogram of product
tonnes of CO2 equivalent per tonne of product

triples.name: abatement dominates
triples.description: worked example on tomatoes: the carbon price triggers a switch from oil heating to a heat pump, the import share rises only moderately and the footprint falls by two thirds; all parameters and results of the example are illustrative assumed values

triples.name: tipping point with partial abatement
triples.description: worked example on tomatoes: with abatement from 3 to 1 the tipping point is an import-share increase of 36 percentage points, i.e. m = 0.46; all parameters and results of the example are illustrative assumed values

triples.name: shift dominates despite abatement
triples.description: worked example on tomatoes: the domestic intensity falls by two thirds, yet the consumption footprint rises by two thirds because the shift term 0.8 * 5 exceeds the abatement term 0.9 * 2; demonstrates that zero abatement is not required for a negative net effect; all parameters and results of the example are illustrative assumed values

triples.name: both effects, abatement wins
triples.description: worked example on tomatoes: 60 percent leakage and still a positive net effect; leakage below 100 percent weakens but does not reverse the measure; all parameters and results of the example are illustrative assumed values

triples.name: steel-like moderate intensity ratio
triples.description: worked example on crude steel: even at an intensity ratio of only 1.5 the net effect turns slightly negative once the import share rises from 20 to 50 percent; the tipping increase is 23 percentage points; all parameters and results of the example are illustrative assumed values

triples.name: shift term must exceed abatement term
triples.description: a negative net effect requires the shift term to exceed the abatement term, not the absence of abatement

triples.name: necessary condition is invariant to abatement
triples.description: the necessary condition eB > e0 is invariant to the amount of domestic abatement; abatement only raises the tipping import increase dm_star

triples.name: negative net effect equals leakage above 100 percent
triples.description: net effect negative is equivalent to leakage rate above 100 percent

triples.name: border carbon adjustment neutralises the shift term
triples.description: a bilateral border carbon adjustment priced at the carbon-price differential times the verified product intensity neutralises the shift term; the only missing input in practice is a verifiable eB per product and origin

triples.name: confidence value
triples.description: The p-value of an assumed value: the subjective probability between 0 and 1 that the tagged estimate is right.

triples.name: net effect
triples.description: dE, the change of the consumption-based footprint per unit of consumption caused by the carbon price; negative is positive for the climate

triples.name: full import
triples.description: the case m = 1, in which the whole consumption is imported

triples.name: net effect at full import
triples.description: the net effect if the whole consumption is imported: ( 1 - m0 ) * ( eB - e0 ), where the abatement intensity eA cancels

triples.name: world market channel
triples.description: lower domestic fossil demand lowers the world market price and so raises the consumption elsewhere
consumption volume is constant; a demand response to higher prices would reduce total emissions and shift all tipping points upward
eB is constant, i.e. the foreign producer does not abate; a foreign carbon price would lower eB and can remove the negative-net-effect region entirely
the fossil world-market channel (lower domestic fossil demand lowering world prices and raising consumption elsewhere) is excluded; it can only worsen the balance
single product, two countries; the import-share response m(carbon price differential) is treated as an input, not modelled

formulas.name: net effect per unit of consumption
formulas.description: change of the consumption-based footprint per kg of product at constant consumption; first summand is the abatement term, second is the shift term

formulas.name: negative net effect condition
formulas.description: the net effect is negative if and only if the shift term exceeds the absolute abatement term; abatement therefore does not need to be zero, only smaller than the shift

formulas.name: tipping import increase (formula)
formulas.description: import-share increase at which the net effect is zero

formulas.name: necessary condition invariance
formulas.description: at full import the abatement intensity eA cancels; a negative net effect is possible for some m <= 1 if and only if eB > e0, independent of how much abatement occurs

formulas.name: leakage rate (formula)
formulas.description: the net effect is negative exactly when the leakage rate is above 1

values.description: Oil-heated winter greenhouse tomatoes, Germany, including road transport to Switzerland. Literature range for heated greenhouse tomatoes is roughly 2 to 6 kg CO2eq per kg; 6 is an upper-range illustration, to be replaced by a verified LCA value.
Heat-pump greenhouse tomatoes on Swiss hydro electricity, remaining emissions from cultivation, substrate, fertiliser, packaging.
EU average blast-furnace route before additional carbon pricing. Order of magnitude consistent with IEA and worldsteel figures; verify against a specific dataset before citing.
Coal-based blast-furnace route with coal-heavy electricity mix, typical for imports from China. Verify against IEA or CBAM default values before citing.
